exposure: Absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) in umbilical cord blood
outcome: Incidence of absolute lymphopenia in umbilical cord blood
Utility in screening for severe combined immunodeficiency disease (SCID)
cohort: The study included 1,550 newborns with gestational ages above 32 weeks, recruited at a tertiary care center in North Karnataka.
finding: Absolute lymphopenia (ALC <2,500/microL) was found in 6.67% of newborns, with causes including prematurity, sepsis, congenital anomalies, and idiopathic factors, and was significantly associated with male sex, consanguinity, need for active resuscitation, lower birth weights, and poorer APGAR scores.
mod_finding: The mode of delivery did not impact lymphopenia rates.
birth_weight: Lymphopenic infants had lower birth weights.
